points.description: Proves P is bijective (injectivity and surjectivity), using the given equation correctly.
points.partial_credit: 1 mark for proving only one of injectivity or surjectivity.

points.description: Proves P(-P(x)) = -x for all rational x.
points.partial_credit: 1 mark for a substantial but incomplete derivation.

points.description: Uses these facts to determine all possible P (or the structure of P(a)+P(-a)), and proves that the set {P(a)+P(-a)} is finite.
points.partial_credit: 1 mark if the family of solutions is correctly described or guessed but finiteness is not fully justified.

points.description: States the correct maximum number of elements of the set (2, as in the model's solution family) and shows it is attained by an explicit valid P.

rubric.notes: Full marks need a complete proof: bijectivity, P(-P(x))=-x, classification giving finiteness, and the correct maximum with an example. Part marks for each proven lemma or correctly guessed solutions. Equivalent wording and alternative valid methods earn the marks.
